comment: The deviations between the Rust base and the web shell that are intentional. They are reported by the comparison — with the concrete difference — but they do not fail the gate. A vector that is not listed here and that deviates fails the gate. The list holds the same vectors as the registry of the crate (core/phomu-conformance/src/lib.rs, KNOWN_DIVERGENCES) — the gate checks that the two lists agree.

divergences.title: The Rust base enters the phase `locked-in`; the web shell does not.
divergences.reason: The core enters the phase `locked-in` when the last expected answer arrives; the reference implementation types the phase but never enters it. The core closes the deviation A6 of the contract — the reveal is only released when the answers are locked in.

divergences.title: The Rust base refuses the reveal until the answers are locked in; the web shell sets the phase.
divergences.reason: The core refuses the reveal until the answers of the round are locked in; the reference implementation lets the store change the phase without the lock. The refusal is the anti-spoiler guarantee of the base.

divergences.title: The Rust base refuses an answer without an active player; the web shell applies the effect of the mode anyway.
divergences.reason: The core refuses an answer when the turn order is empty — there is nobody to attribute the answer to. The reference implementation evaluates the mode and applies its effect without recording the answer.

divergences.title: The web shell can set the phase `locked-in`; the base refuses the transition.
divergences.reason: The core enters the declared phase `locked-in` only when the expected answers are submitted; the reference implementation sets the phase from the store. The vector is marked as not portable in the corpus.

divergences.title: The base answers an unknown player with a typed error; the web shell ignores it silently.
divergences.reason: The core answers with the typed error `UnknownPlayer`; the reference implementation ignores the unknown identifier. The vector is marked as not portable in the corpus.

divergences.title: The base answers an unknown year with a typed error; the web shell ignores it silently.
divergences.reason: The core answers with the typed error `InvalidAnswer`; the reference implementation ignores the unknown year. The vector is marked as not portable in the corpus.

divergences.title: The base recomputes the team scores after the team shuffle; the web shell keeps them (deviation A8).
divergences.reason: The core recomputes the team scores after the redistribution of the players, so that the team score is the sum of the points of its members (GAME-007). The reference implementation leaves the team scores untouched (GAME-CONTRACT § 6.2, deviation A8). The vector is marked as not portable in the corpus.
